title: Arrays & Hashing
description: The foundation of DSA. Learn to use HashMaps and HashSets to solve problems in O(1) lookup time.
tip: Always ask: Can I trade space for time using a HashMap?

hardProblems.title: First Missing Positive
hardProblems.hint: Use the array itself as a hash table by placing each number at its correct index.

hardProblems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
hardProblems.hint: Use a HashSet. For each number, check if it's the start of a sequence (num-1 not in set).

hardProblems.title: Minimum Window Substring
hardProblems.hint: Use two HashMaps to track character frequencies + sliding window.

hardProblems.title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
hardProblems.hint: Sliding window with word-level frequency maps. Words are same length — use that.

title: Two Pointers
description: Use two pointers moving towards each other or in the same direction to solve problems efficiently.
tip: Works best on sorted arrays. If unsorted, sort first then apply two pointers.

hardProblems.title: Trapping Rain Water
hardProblems.hint: Two pointers from each end. Track leftMax and rightMax. Water = min(leftMax, rightMax) - height.

hardProblems.title: 4Sum
hardProblems.hint: Fix two numbers, then use two pointers for the remaining pair. Handle duplicate skipping.

hardProblems.title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
hardProblems.hint: Find the leftmost and rightmost positions where order breaks. Expand using min/max tracking.

title: Sliding Window
description: Maintain a window of elements and slide it across the array. Perfect for substring problems.
tip: If the problem says 'contiguous subarray' or 'substring', think Sliding Window immediately.

hardProblems.title: Minimum Window Substring
hardProblems.hint: Expand right to cover all chars, then shrink left to minimize window. Use character count maps.

hardProblems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
hardProblems.hint: Use a Monotonic Deque (decreasing). Front = max of window. Remove out-of-window indices.

hardProblems.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
hardProblems.hint: Variable window + HashMap tracking char frequencies. Shrink when distinct count > k.

hardProblems.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
hardProblems.hint: exactly(K) = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1). Use sliding window for atMost function.

title: Stack
description: LIFO data structure. Essential for parentheses matching and monotonic stack problems.
tip: If you need to match or track 'most recent' elements, use a Stack.

hardProblems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
hardProblems.hint: Monotonic increasing stack. For each bar, find left and right boundaries where shorter bars exist.

hardProblems.title: Maximal Rectangle
hardProblems.hint: Build histogram heights row by row, then solve 'Largest Rectangle in Histogram' for each row.

hardProblems.title: Basic Calculator
hardProblems.hint: Use stack for sign tracking. Push current result and sign when '(' is seen, pop when ')'.

hardProblems.title: Longest Valid Parentheses
hardProblems.hint: Stack stores indices. Push -1 as base. On match, length = i - stack.peek().

title: Binary Search
description: Divide and conquer on sorted data. Reduces O(n) to O(log n).
tip: If the array is sorted or the answer is monotonic, Binary Search is the key.

hardProblems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
hardProblems.hint: Binary search on the smaller array. Partition both arrays so left halves equal right halves.

hardProblems.title: Split Array Largest Sum
hardProblems.hint: Binary search on the answer (max subarray sum). Use greedy to check if k splits are feasible.

hardProblems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
hardProblems.hint: Binary search but handle duplicates: when nums[mid] == nums[right], just shrink right by 1.

hardProblems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
hardProblems.hint: Binary search on the value range. Count elements ≤ mid using sorted row/column property.

title: Linked Lists
description: Master pointer manipulation. Problems involve reversing, merging, and detecting cycles.
tip: Draw the pointers on paper. Visualizing next pointers prevents bugs.

hardProblems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
hardProblems.hint: Use a Min-Heap of size k. Always poll smallest, add its next node. O(N log k).

hardProblems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
hardProblems.hint: Count k nodes ahead. If enough, reverse that segment. Connect previous tail to new head.

hardProblems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
hardProblems.hint: Interleave cloned nodes: A→A'→B→B'. Set random pointers using A'.random = A.random.next.

title: Trees (BFS & DFS)
description: Hierarchical data structures. Use DFS and BFS to traverse and solve tree problems.
tip: DFS = Recursion/Stack. BFS = Queue. Know when to use which.

hardProblems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
hardProblems.hint: DFS returns max single-branch sum. At each node, update global max with left + node + right.

hardProblems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
hardProblems.hint: Preorder traversal with null markers. Use queue for deserialization.

hardProblems.title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
hardProblems.hint: BFS with (col, row) tracking. Use TreeMap sorted by column, then by row.

hardProblems.title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
hardProblems.hint: Compare left and right depth. If equal, nodes = 2^h − 1. Otherwise recurse. O(log²n).

title: Graphs
description: Nodes and edges. Learn BFS, DFS, topological sort, and union-find.
tip: Build an adjacency list first, then decide BFS vs DFS based on the problem.

hardProblems.title: Word Ladder
hardProblems.hint: BFS level by level. Each word connects to all words differing by 1 char. Use wildcard patterns.

hardProblems.title: Alien Dictionary
hardProblems.hint: Build a directed graph from adjacent word pairs. Topological sort gives the ordering.

hardProblems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
hardProblems.hint: Modified Bellman-Ford with K+1 iterations. Or BFS with priority queue tracking (cost, node, stops).

hardProblems.title: Critical Connections in a Network
hardProblems.hint: Tarjan's algorithm. Track discovery time and low-link values. Bridge = disc[u] < low[v].

hardProblems.title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
hardProblems.hint: BFS with state (row, col, remainingK). visited[row][col][k] prevents revisits.

title: Dynamic Programming
description: Break problems into overlapping subproblems. Use memoization or tabulation.
tip: Define the state clearly. Ask: What choices do I have at each step?

hardProblems.title: Edit Distance
hardProblems.hint: dp[i][j] = min ops to convert word1[0..i] to word2[0..j]. Three choices: insert, delete, replace.

hardProblems.title: Regular Expression Matching
hardProblems.hint: dp[i][j] = does s[0..i] match p[0..j]. Handle '.' and '*' cases. '*' can match 0 or more.

hardProblems.title: Burst Balloons
hardProblems.hint: Think backwards — which balloon is burst LAST? dp[i][j] = max coins for range (i, j).

hardProblems.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
hardProblems.hint: DFS + memoization. memo[i][j] = longest path starting at (i,j). Only go to strictly greater neighbors.

hardProblems.title: Palindrome Partitioning II
hardProblems.hint: dp[i] = min cuts for s[0..i]. Precompute isPalin[i][j]. dp[i] = min(dp[j-1] + 1) for all valid j.

title: Backtracking
description: Explore all possibilities incrementally. Used in permutations and combinations.
tip: Think of it as DFS on a decision tree. Prune early for efficiency.

hardProblems.title: N-Queens
hardProblems.hint: Place queens row by row. Track columns, diagonals (r-c), and anti-diagonals (r+c) used.

hardProblems.title: Sudoku Solver
hardProblems.hint: Try 1-9 in each empty cell. Validate row, col, and 3x3 box. Backtrack on failure.

hardProblems.title: Word Search II
hardProblems.hint: Build a Trie from words. DFS on grid with Trie pruning. Remove found words from Trie.

hardProblems.title: Palindrome Partitioning
hardProblems.hint: Backtrack: at each position, try all substrings. If palindrome, recurse on remainder.

title: Heap / Priority Queue
description: Efficiently find min/max elements. Essential for K-largest problems.
tip: Use a Min-Heap when you need the K largest, and Max-Heap for K smallest.

hardProblems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
hardProblems.hint: Two heaps: Max-heap for lower half, Min-heap for upper half. Balance sizes. Median from tops.

hardProblems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
hardProblems.hint: Min-heap of size k. Poll smallest node, push its next. O(N log k) total.

hardProblems.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
hardProblems.hint: Min-heap with one element from each list. Track global max. Range = [heap.peek(), globalMax].

hardProblems.title: IPO
hardProblems.hint: Sort by capital needed. Max-heap of available profits. Greedily pick max profit k times.

title: Greedy
description: Make the locally optimal choice at each step. Common in interval problems.
tip: Sort the input first, then greedily pick the best option at each step.

hardProblems.title: Candy
hardProblems.hint: Two passes: left-to-right (increasing neighbor gets more), right-to-left (same). Take max.

hardProblems.title: Task Scheduler
hardProblems.hint: Most frequent task dictates. Idle slots = (maxFreq - 1) * n. Fill with other tasks.

hardProblems.title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
hardProblems.hint: Max-heap of passed stations' fuel. When out of fuel, greedily refuel from the best passed station.

hardProblems.title: Patching Array
hardProblems.hint: Track max reachable sum. If next num > reach+1, patch with reach+1. Otherwise, extend reach.

title: Bit Manipulation
description: Use XOR, AND, OR, and shifting to solve problems at the bit level.
tip: XOR of a number with itself = 0. XOR with 0 = number itself.

hardProblems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
hardProblems.hint: Build a bit Trie. For each number, greedily choose opposite bit at each level for max XOR.

hardProblems.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
hardProblems.hint: Find the common prefix of m and n in binary. Right-shift both until equal, then left-shift back.

hardProblems.title: Total Hamming Distance
hardProblems.hint: For each bit position, count 0s and 1s. Contribution = count0 × count1. Sum all 32 bits.

title: Intervals
description: Problems involving ranges [start, end]. Essential for scheduling problems.
tip: Always sort intervals by start time first. Then iterate and merge.

hardProblems.title: Insert Interval
hardProblems.hint: Add all intervals before overlap, merge overlapping ones, add all after. One pass O(n).

hardProblems.title: Employee Free Time
hardProblems.hint: Flatten all intervals, sort by start. Gaps between merged intervals = free time.

hardProblems.title: Meeting Rooms III
hardProblems.hint: Two heaps: available rooms (min-heap by ID) and busy rooms (min-heap by end time). Simulate.

hardProblems.title: Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals
hardProblems.hint: Use TreeMap. On add, check if num merges with adjacent intervals. getIntervals returns all values.
